# vk v0.6.0

Date: 2026-10-26. Status: Experimental development release.
Cargo package: `vkrust` version `0.6.0+1.4.365`. Rust library/import: `vk`. License: MIT.

## Scope

Complete generated construction coverage for all 1,552 concrete records/unions
and 8,333 native fields in the pinned paired Vulkan/StdVideo registries. The
generator emits 5,450 construction methods. Native ABI and coverage of all 842
selected commands, including core Vulkan 1.0–1.4, are unchanged. Free functions
and wrapper methods continue to share cached dispatch and operation bodies.

## Changes

- Generate checked byte payloads, SPIR-V word slices with byte-sized codeSize,
  sample masks, fixed UUID pairs and native-width video counts.
- Support optional parallel arrays, initialized writable outputs, reviewed
  parent/cross-record capacities and direct/pointer-table alternatives.
- Generate union member setters and typed layer-setting payloads. Propagate
  exclusive borrows through records, unions and aliases without changing C ABI.
- Preserve direct native-count setters for null-query, dynamic-state and
  extension-payload paths. These do not revalidate earlier pointer extents.
- Audit every native field in a generated inventory, independently compared
  with both registries. Unknown sized relationships fail generation.
- Keep explicit unsafe setters for 44 unbounded opaque/foreign fields; registry
  metadata cannot establish their extent or native retention lifetime.

The 2,657 registry type declarations are not a record-wrapper completion count.
The 1,565 lifetime-bearing declarations comprise 1,313 records/unions and 252
aliases. Another 239 records/unions are plain values; the remaining 853 entries
are other aliases, enums, flags, handles, callbacks and base/external types.

## Compatibility and migration

Use `vk = { package = "vkrust", version = "0.6" }`. The suffix `+1.4.365`
identifies pinned Vulkan headers, not a minimum driver version. Rust 1.98.1 and
edition 2024 remain the declared baseline. The loader is enabled by default;
the work-in-progress allocator remains opt-in.

This minor release extends lifetime parameters and removes Copy/Clone from
additional records that retain exclusive storage, including by-value containers.
Declare stored borrowed records as `Type<'a>` and initialize hidden markers with
`Type { field: value, ..Default::default() }`. Use `std::array::from_fn` for fresh
non-Copy array elements and `std::slice::from_ref` for borrowed single records.
Exclusive union fields use ManuallyDrop while preserving native layout.

Keep backing storage live through the record's last use. Writable slices must
already be initialized. Pointer tables borrow the table, not their pointees.
Pass matching capacity records to native output queries and distinguish supplied
capacity from returned required size. No safe accessor derives a slice from a
public pointer and driver-written size. Raw field edits remain available.

## Verification and limits

The implementation checkpoint passed 3,201 workspace tests/doctests, including
1,552 generated record contracts and 11 negative borrowing/unsafe compiler
fixtures. Independent checks cover 1,447 C/Rust records, 9,267 layout/value
comparisons, 348 bitfield comparisons, all 842 Rust PFNs and 775 C prototypes.
The other 67 protected C prototypes remain unqualified by that header set.
Generation, strict Clippy, minimal/default configurations, rustdoc/native search
and extracted-package consumers passed. Intel/Mesa instance/device smoke tests
passed on the recorded Vulkan 1.2 profile.

Release CI independently verifies the actual sanitized commit, Cargo archive,
Windows/macOS host tests, pinned C/VMA oracles and explicit Lavapipe workloads.
Consult the workflow and release artifacts for release-specific results.

Borrowing covers host record storage. Native resource ownership, asynchronous
pointer retention, Vulkan valid usage and GPU completion remain caller duties.
The allocator remains Experimental and is not VMA-equivalent. Physical Vulkan
1.3/1.4, WSI, video, ray tracing, external interoperability and broader device
qualification remain open. No Miri qualification or performance advantage is
claimed. See [qualification and limitations](../qualification.md).

## Distribution

The release tag is `v0.6.0`; the full registry version is `0.6.0+1.4.365`.
Private/public histories retain distinct commit IDs. Public snapshots exclude
private history, engineering documents and editor/agent configuration. The
release workflow publishes the verified archive, checks downloaded registry
bytes, and attaches documentation, checksums and build evidence to the GitHub
development release. Existing tags and registry versions remain immutable.
